exposure: mature cystic teratoma (MCT) with squamous cell cancer (SCC)
left ovarian cystectomy via elective caesarean section
debulking surgery without total pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy
outcome: retroperitoneal spread to para-aortic lymph nodes
FIGO IA staging for ovarian malignancy
confirmation of metastases in para-aortic lymph nodes
cohort: A 35-year-old multiparous pregnant woman diagnosed with an ovarian tumor in early pregnancy, which was subsequently found to be squamous cell cancer originating from a mature cystic teratoma.
finding: This case illustrates the rapid retroperitoneal spread of squamous cell cancer originating from a mature cystic teratoma, even after initial staging suggested no extraovarian disease, highlighting the need for comprehensive staging procedures including lymphadenectomy.
